scope: Kubernetes v1.36.1 runs two case-owned copies of a small promotion API. Both receive the same case-minted ServiceAccount token and fixed inert decision; the disabled gate accepts it, while the enabled gate uses authentication.k8s.io/v1 TokenReview with a fixed audience and an exact reviewer allowlist. The enabled gate rejects wrong-audience, missing, and authenticated-but-unapproved identities and accepts the allowlisted reviewer. This proves the Kubernetes token identity/audience boundary for one inert decision only; external OIDC/SSO, human session binding, audit binding, and deployed workflow coverage need separate evidence.

checks.claim: With the deployed gate disabled, the same fixed decision accepts its case-minted wrong-audience credential
The deployed gate rejects that credential because TokenReview does not authenticate it for the promotion audience
A different authenticated ServiceAccount cannot approve the fixed decision
The deployed gate rejects a request with no reviewer credential
The allowlisted reviewer is authenticated for the promotion audience and accepted
